children: It seemed that after a run of surprisingly hearty job results that Canada was almost due for a reality check, says Bank of Montreal's Douglas Porter. August's job report was undoubtedly soft, but far from a shock, and in part reflects the ongoing sag in the labor force population, the economist says. A cooldown in employment and average wages will reinforce the Bank of Canada's holding pattern, and should calm some of the extreme rate-increase pricing in the market, he says. Overall employment was down 41,700 for the month, ending a string of upbeat job gains, while the unemployment rate held steady at 6.4%. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)
